formalObservation.Composition:
The composition is organized within a dark, approximately rectangular perimeter. Several distinct forms occupy the interior:

- centrally positioned spherical/head-like form
- smaller human-like figure at lower left
- large rectangular or box-like form at right
- horizontally elongated form at bottom
- suspended horizontal cylindrical form near the upper portion

The elements are distributed across the vertical field rather than concentrated into a single central figure.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
- Circular / spherical anthropomorphic form
- Smaller human-like figure
- Rectangular structure
- Elongated horizontal structure
- Suspended cylindrical form
formalObservation.Visible Anatomical Features:
Central circular form:
- one large eye
- open mouth
- multiple triangular tooth-like marks

Smaller left-hand figure:
- head
- eye
- nose / facial projection
- mouth
- torso
- lower circular form beneath the figure
formalObservation.Structural / Mechanical Forms:
- Horizontal cylindrical element at top
- Two narrow vertical lines connecting the cylinder to the central circular form
- Rectangular box-like structure at right
- Horizontal elongated structure at bottom
- Multiple small circular forms beneath or adjacent to structures
formalObservation.Repeated Geometric Forms:
- Circles
- Rectangles
- Horizontal bands
- Vertical lines
- Triangular marks
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
- dense parallel hatching
- broad charcoal strokes
- darker filled areas
- repeated linear marks
- contour drawing
- localized smudging / tonal buildup

The perimeter is significantly darker and denser than much of the interior field.
formalObservation.Tonal Distribution:
High contrast.

Large areas of white paper remain visible between comparatively dense charcoal structures.
formalObservation.Figure–Ground Relationship: Strong separation between the charcoal structures and the largely unworked paper ground.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Strong use of enclosing borders.
- Combination of circular, rectangular and elongated forms.
- Multiple independent forms occupy the same pictorial field.
- Repetition of circular elements.
- Hatching functions as both contour construction and tonal information.
- Anatomical and structural forms coexist without conventional proportional relationships.
